title: Link worker social prescribing: an umbrella review of wellbeing, loneliness, consultation and cost outcomes
subtitle: Umbrella review for an integrated care board funding decision
statement: An integrated care board must decide whether to fund more social prescribing link workers, but published reviews disagree: some report better wellbeing and fewer GP consultations, others find the evidence too weak, and the same small evaluations recur across reviews. A primary care network needs an umbrella review that appraises the existing reviews, measures their overlap and summarises effects on wellbeing, loneliness, consultation rates and costs, including for people with complex needs.
whoAffected: People referred to link workers for loneliness, low mood, money and housing problems, long-term conditions and frequent attendance; link workers; GPs; and the commissioners deciding on funding.
whatHurts: Funding decisions made on overstated evidence divert money from other services, while withdrawing a service that helps people with complex needs would leave them without support.
currentPractice: Four link workers take about 1,600 referrals a year; the commissioning board has conflicting review summaries and no appraisal of their overlap or quality.
whyNow: The commissioning board decides on link worker funding on 26 February 2027.
constraints: No funding; about 12 weeks of part-time work; report to the commissioning board in February 2027.
patientCenteredGoal: People with social needs get support that demonstrably helps them, and commissioners know which groups benefit.
summary: Problem framed as an umbrella review; the reply shortens the constraints in its own words.
